intent: Research sealed counterfactual lead MS-0122 as an Evidence-first DRAM-versus-NAND cycle decomposition across 2016-2026. Test the alternative to treating DRAM and NAND as one synchronized cycle by preserving common macro/supplier-cycle direction separately from product-specific turning points, severity, technology cadence, supply elasticity and end-market mix. Reuse already-grounded 2017 competing-mechanism, 2022 inventory-amplification and 2024 recovery-decomposition packets; add only same-source or otherwise directly comparable evidence that establishes dated lead/lag or divergence. Do not manufacture a correlation coefficient, assume same-quarter turning points, or convert aggregate co-movement into identical causal mechanisms.
rationale_summary: Existing packets already show that DRAM and NAND can share broad up/down phases while carrying different mechanisms: the 2017 upcycle packet separates DRAM wafer-capacity expectations from NAND transition-related effective-supply loss; the 2022 packet separates inventory amplification states; the 2024 packet separates conventional recovery from HBM/enterprise overlays. MS-0122 therefore needs only compact, directly comparable turning-point evidence. Same-source TrendForce observations provide clean anchors where NAND led DRAM at the 2018 downturn and 2023 recovery turns and where NAND was explicitly described as more severe during the 2022 downturn.
